question: Today is Wednesday 3 December 2025. My agent gave me written notice seven days ahead that I must be home for a smoke alarm check on a weekday between 10 am and 12:30 pm, or pay a $90 fee to rebook. The agent has a key to the place. Do I have to be there myself to let the inspector in, and can they charge me the $90?
answer:
**Short answer:** Based on the documents, you don't have to be there yourself for the agent to enter, as long as the entry follows the proper procedure. The documents don't mention any $90 rebooking fee, so I can't confirm the agent can charge it.

**What the law says**

- **Entry rights:** A provider or agent may enter for a duty under the Act, with at least 24 hours' written notice, between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. on any day except a public holiday [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Smoke alarm testing is one of the provider's duties: smoke alarms must be tested at least once every 12 months [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The notice must be in writing and state why entry is wanted [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Your notice of seven days, for a weekday morning, falls within these rules [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Your duty:** A renter must permit a person exercising a right of entry under these rules to enter [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The documents don't say that you personally must be home. They also don't say the agent's key changes anything. Nothing in the excerpts I retrieved requires you to be present or addresses key-holding.
- **Manner of entry:** The entry must be reasonable, and the person must not stay longer than needed for the purpose without your consent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **The $90 fee:** I found no provision in the Act or the Regulations allowing a rebooking fee for a missed entry. The documents don't cover this, so I can't say whether it is lawful.

**What you can do or ask**

- **Ask the agent** to point to the provision that allows the $90 fee, and to confirm the notice was delivered by post or personally between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Ask to schedule around your availability.** You can apply to the Tribunal for an order specifying or limiting when entry may occur [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **If entry isn't done properly,** you can apply to the Tribunal for an order restraining the provider and agent from entering for a specified period [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Any damage to your goods during entry** can be the subject of a Tribunal compensation application [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

**Versions applied:** Today is 3 December 2025. The *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* (Authorised Version 111, in force from 25 November 2025) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf) and the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021* (Authorised Version 005, in force from 25 November 2025) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf) were the versions in force on that date.

must-mention.reason: Yes. Both points are covered. On presence, the answer says "you don't have to be there yourself for the agent to enter, as long as the entry follows the proper procedure" and notes the renter's duty is to "permit a person exercising a right of entry." On notice, it says smoke alarm testing is the provider's duty, that entry needs "at least 24 hours' written notice, between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.," and that the seven days' notice "falls within these rules."

must-not-say.reason: Yes. The answer never says the renter must be home or must pay the fee; it states "you don't have to be there yourself for the agent to enter" and "I can't confirm the agent can charge it," noting no provision allows a rebooking fee.

version-cited.reason: Yes: the answer names the 'Residential Tenancies Act 1997 (Authorised Version 111, in force from 25 November 2025)' with link 97-109aa111 and the 'Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021 (Authorised Version 005, in force from 25 November 2025)' with link 21-3sra005, and every rule it applies is cited to those in-force versions.

question: It's the middle of January 2026 (Thursday the 15th). My rent app charges a fee when I pay by card. The app is run by a payments company my agent uses, and it's that company that charges the card fee. There's also a manual bank transfer option with no fee, but it's slower. Can the app charge me the card fee? Does it matter whether the fee goes to the app company or to the agent?
answer:
**Short answer:** On the documents I found, the agent must make a no-extra-cost payment method reasonably available and must disclose card fees before you agree to use a method. The app company's own fee is restricted by a rule that doesn't take effect until 31 March 2026, so it doesn't clearly bar the fee on 15 January 2026. The documents don't say whether the fee is lawful in every other respect.

**Versions applied:** The *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* (version 111, in force from 25 November 2025 to 29 June 2026) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf) and the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021* (version 005, in force from 25 November 2025 to 9 February 2026) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf) were both in force on 15 January 2026.

## What the law says

- **Fee-free method must be available:** The agent must "ensure that a rent payment method that incurs no additional costs (other than bank fees or account fees payable on the renter's bank account) is reasonably available to the renter" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Penalties are 80 penalty units for a natural person or 400 for a body corporate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Disclosure before you agree:** The agent must give you information about "any costs (including third party transaction fees...)" before you consent to a payment method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). A card fee charged by a third-party payments company is a third-party transaction fee.
- **Electronic payment methods:** The agent must also permit Centrepay and any prescribed payment method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The prescribed method is electronic funds transfer [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). A bank transfer may fall within this, but the documents don't say whether it must be instant.
- **Fee restriction on businesses (s 51A):** A business other than a provider, provider's agent, or authorised deposit-taking institution must not demand or receive a fee for a prescribed matter relating to rent payment [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The agent is expressly excluded from this rule [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf), so it applies to the payments company, not the agent.
- **Prescribed matters (reg 21C):** Rent payment is listed as a prescribed matter, but only "other than payment surcharge fees permitted under any other Act" [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). Regulation 21C "has effect on and after 31 March 2026" [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). So on 15 January 2026, this restriction isn't yet in effect, and the documents don't show whether any other Act permits a surcharge.
- **Prohibited term:** Regulation 10(3)(d) says it is a prohibited term to require rent in advance "by a payment method which requires additional costs (other than bank fees or account fees...)" [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). This matters if your agreement requires card payment.

## Does it matter who gets the fee?

Yes, in one respect. Under s 51A, the restriction targets the payments company, not the agent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). But the agent's duties under s 42(4) and s 42(7) apply regardless of who collects the fee [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). If the agent receives or passes on the fee, the agent is still responsible for offering a no-extra-cost method and disclosing the fee.

## What you can do or ask

1. **Ask the agent in writing** to confirm the card fee amount and that it is a third-party transaction fee, as required by s 42(7) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
2. **Ask that the fee-free bank transfer be made available** as a reasonably available method under s 42(4) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Slowness alone isn't addressed in the documents.
3. **Check your agreement.** The standard form asks the provider to tick available payment methods and notes that at least one fee-free method must be permitted [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).
4. **Ask about Centrepay** as an alternative, since the agent must permit it under s 42(5) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
5. **Keep records and get receipts.** Written receipts are required for rent payments in certain cases under s 43 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). I didn't retrieve the full text of s 43(1), so I can't confirm the detailed requirements.

**Limits:** The documents don't say how to complain or enforce these rules. I also only have the Regulations version that ends on 9 February 2026, so I can't confirm whether reg 21C's wording changed after that. If you want to rely on the 31 March 2026 restriction, check the current version of the Regulations.

must-mention.reason: Yes. Both points are covered. The answer says a fee-free method must be 'reasonably available' and treats the fee-free bank transfer as a candidate for that ("Ask that the fee-free bank transfer be made available as a reasonably available method under s 42(4)... Slowness alone isn't addressed in the documents"). It also states that reg 21C "has effect on and after 31 March 2026" and so "isn't yet in effect" on 15 January 2026.

must-not-say.reason: Yes. The answer does not claim the fee is already banned: it says reg 21C "has effect on and after 31 March 2026" so "on 15 January 2026, this restriction isn't yet in effect." It also affirms rather than denies a fee-free rule, stating the agent must "ensure that a rent payment method that incurs no additional costs ... is reasonably available to the renter."

version-cited.reason: Yes. The answer names the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 as "version 111" (link 97-109aa111) and the Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021 as "version 005" (link 21-3sra005), both in force on 15 January 2026, and it relies on no other version, treating reg 21C from version 005 as not yet in effect.

question: This is happening now, on 15 October 2019. I signed a lease and picked up the keys, but before moving in I found damp, mould and rotting timber in the house. I haven't moved any of my things in or stayed there yet. What are my options? Can I cancel, ask for repairs, or ask for lower rent?
answer:
**Short answer:** Under the Act as it stood on 15 October 2019, you may be able to refuse to move in, ask for repairs, and withhold rent until you move in. Cancelling is possible but depends on whether the defects meet a specific legal ground. The documents I retrieved don't settle every point, so I flag the gaps below.

**Which law applies:** The retrieved document is the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997*, Authorised Version No. 088, incorporating amendments as at 2 July 2019. It was in force from 2 July 2019 to 3 December 2019, so it covers 15 October 2019 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

## What the Act says

- On the day you are due to move in, the landlord must ensure the premises are vacant and reasonably clean. You are not required to enter premises that don't comply [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 65).
- If they don't comply, you don't have to pay rent from the agreed occupation day until you actually move in [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 65(3)).
- The landlord must ensure the premises are maintained in good repair [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 68(1)).
- A tenancy ends before you take possession if you give the landlord a notice of termination on the ground that the premises are not in good repair, or are unfit for human habitation [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 226).
- The endnotes show amendments that would change s 68 to require premises be "in good repair" and "in a reasonably fit and suitable condition for occupation," whether or not you knew of the disrepair. They also add mould or damp caused by the building structure to the definition of urgent repairs [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The excerpts don't state when these amendments commenced, so I can't confirm they applied on 15 October 2019.

## Your options

**1. Cancel**
- Section 226 may allow you to end the agreement if you haven't moved in and give notice on the grounds above [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- Whether damp, mould and rotting timber amount to "not in good repair" or "unfit for human habitation" is not answered by the documents. The documents also don't give a form or deadline for the notice.

**2. Ask for repairs**
- *Non-urgent repairs:* If you give the landlord written notice and they don't carry out the repairs within 14 days, you can apply to the Director to investigate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 74). You can then apply to the Tribunal for an order requiring repairs [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 75, s 76).
- *Urgent repairs:* You may arrange urgent repairs if you have taken reasonable steps to get the landlord to do them immediately and they can't or won't. The landlord must reimburse the reasonable cost or $1000, whichever is less [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 72). You can also apply to the Tribunal, which must hear the application within 2 business days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 73). The documents don't say whether these tenant-repair rights apply before you move in.
- If the landlord fails to comply with the duty to maintain premises, you can give a breach of duty notice. It must be in writing, specify the breach, give details of the loss, and require the breach be remedied or compensation paid within the required time, which is 14 days for this duty [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 207, s 208).

**3. Ask for lower rent**
- *No rent until move-in:* If the premises fail the cleanliness requirement in s 65, you don't pay rent until you actually move in [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The documents don't clearly say whether damp, mould or rot count as failing that requirement. Section 65 refers to being vacant and reasonably clean, not structural defects.
- *Compensation as a rent reduction:* If the Tribunal orders compensation, the order may specify that it be a refund or reduction of rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 212(5)). That follows a breach of duty notice and an application under s 209, and the Tribunal can consider factors including whether you have mitigated the loss [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 211).
- The "excessive rent" process in ss 45–47 is tied to rent increases or reduced services, so it doesn't clearly fit your situation [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

## Practical points

- **Condition report:** If you pay a bond, the landlord must give you a condition report before you move in. Within 3 business days of moving in you must return a copy, signed or with an endorsement if you disagree [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 35). A signed report is conclusive evidence of state of repair, unless you dispute a statement with an endorsement [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) (s 36). Don't sign a report that understates the defects.
- **Document everything:** Put your complaint in writing and keep photos and dates.

This is general information based only on the excerpts retrieved, not legal advice. For a decision on cancelling, I'd recommend getting advice before giving any notice.

must-mention.reason: Yes. Every required point is stated. (1) The s 226 cancellation ground is given directly: "A tenancy ends before you take possession if you give the landlord a notice of termination on the ground that the premises are not in good repair, or are unfit for human habitation." (2) The answer cites the s 68 good-repair duty, sets out how to request repairs, and presents urgent repairs as an option, noting mould or damp from the building structure. (3) It says cancelling "depends on whether the defects meet a specific legal ground," separates s 65's "vacant and reasonably clean" test from structural defects, and recommends keeping photos.

must-not-say.reason: Yes: neither failure condition is asserted. The answer mentions the later mould and damp amendments only to say "The excerpts don't state when these amendments commenced, so I can't confirm they applied on 15 October 2019," and rather than saying the renter must move in and pay rent, it says "You are not required to enter premises that don't comply" and "you don't have to pay rent from the agreed occupation day until you actually move in."

version-cited.reason: Yes. The answer names the 'Residential Tenancies Act 1997, Authorised Version No. 088, incorporating amendments as at 2 July 2019', which is the version in force on 15 October 2019. Every rule it applies (ss 35, 36, 65, 68(1), 72 with the $1000 cap, 73–76, 207–212, 226) comes from that version. It mentions the not-yet-operative amendments (s 68 'reasonably fit and suitable' and mould or damp as an urgent repair) only to say it cannot confirm they applied on that date. It never presents them as law or as a step the user can take, so deleting them would not change the substance of the options.

question: I am asking on Tuesday 8 November 2022. I signed a lease through an agency and paid the bond and the first month's rent. Now, a week after I signed, the agent says the owner will manage the place themselves and has sent me new bank details for the rent. What should I check before I pay into the new account?
answer:
Under the **Residential Tenancies Act 1997 (version 101, in force from 7 September 2022)** [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf) and the **Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021 (version 002, in force from 1 June 2022)** [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf), both of which applied on 8 November 2022, the rent payment method is set by your agreement, and the owner cannot switch it on their own.

**What the law says**

- Rent is payable at the place in your agreement, or at the premises if none is specified. Otherwise, it is payable in the manner specified in the agreement [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- The owner and you can change how rent is payable, but only **by agreement** [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- Before you consent to a payment method, the owner or agent must tell you about any costs you may incur by using it, including third-party transaction fees [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- The owner must ensure a rent payment method with no additional costs (other than your own bank or account fees) is reasonably available to you [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- If the agent's details or other contact information change, the owner must notify you in writing within 7 days after the change [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The standard form also says the rental provider must notify the renter within 7 days if agent details change [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).
- Rent must be receipted: a receipt is required immediately for in-person payments, or within 5 business days if you request one for other payments. It must be signed and state your name, the premises, the date, the period, the amount, and that it is rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- The bond is separate from rent. The provider must lodge it with the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority within 10 business days of receiving it, and the Authority must send you a receipt within 7 days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). If you don't receive a receipt within 15 business days of paying, you may notify the Authority [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The standard form gives the Authority's contact as rtba@justice.vic.gov.au or 1300 137 164 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).

**What to check before paying the new account**

1. **Your lease's payment terms.** Find the payment method and place written into your agreement. Any change needs your agreement under the Act [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
2. **Written notice of the change.** Ask for written notice that the owner is now managing the property, with the owner's full name and address for service of documents, and an emergency contact number [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The Act requires these details when there is no agent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
3. **Costs of the new method.** Ask what fees apply to paying that account and confirm it is not a fee-charging method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
4. **Bond status.** Confirm your bond was lodged with the Authority and that you have its receipt. The new account is for rent only. Do not pay bond money into it [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
5. **Receipts.** Confirm that you will receive a signed receipt for each rent payment [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).

**What you can ask for or do**

- You do not have to accept the new account just because the agent asks. Rent is payable as your agreement specifies unless you agree to a change [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- If you agree to change the method, put the agreement in writing and keep a copy.
- If the owner refuses to provide the information above or the bond receipt, you can raise it with the owner and the agent, and contact the Authority about the bond [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).

**What the documents don't cover**

- The documents do not say how to verify bank details or prevent payment-redirection fraud. Independently confirm the owner's identity and the new account (for example, by calling the owner on a number you already have) before paying. This is general advice, not from the retrieved documents.
- The documents do not say whether handing management from the agency to the owner counts as a transfer of rights and duties that requires notice to the Authority under section 424 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). Ask the agent or check with the Authority.
- I don't have your lease, so I can't confirm what payment method it specifies.

must-mention.reason: Yes (pass). All three points are covered. (1) The answer asks for written notice of 'the owner's full name and address for service of documents, and an emergency contact number', says the Act requires these when there is no agent, and says the owner must notify changes 'in writing within 7 days after the change'. (2) It states the bond must be lodged with the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority and advises the renter to 'Confirm your bond was lodged with the Authority and that you have its receipt'. (3) It says rent payment can change 'only by agreement' and advises to 'Independently confirm the owner's identity and the new account (for example, by calling the owner on a number you already have) before paying.'

question: Today is Wednesday 3 December 2025. My agent gave me written notice seven days ahead that I must be home for a smoke alarm check on a weekday between 10 am and 12:30 pm, or pay a $90 fee to rebook. The agent has a key to the place. Do I have to be there myself to let the inspector in, and can they charge me the $90?

- **Purpose and notice:** A provider or agent may enter to carry out a duty under the Act [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). A smoke alarm check is part of the provider's duty to ensure smoke alarms are tested at least once every 12 months, so this purpose applies [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). For that purpose, entry between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. on a day that isn't a public holiday requires at least 24 hours' notice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The Regulations say the renter must allow entry where the provider has followed proper procedure [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).
- **The agent's key:** Having a key doesn't by itself permit entry. An agent who enters otherwise than in accordance with the entry Division, without reasonable excuse, commits an offence with a penalty of 60 penalty units [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Manner of entry:** The person entering must act reasonably and must not stay longer than necessary for the purpose without your consent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

Whether a time window and a requirement to be home are reasonable is not addressed in the documents I retrieved.

**Can they charge $90?** The retrieved documents don't mention a rebooking fee. The table of contents of the Act lists "Certain charges prohibited" (s 51) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf), but I did not retrieve its text, so I can't tell you whether this fee is allowed.

question: It's the middle of January 2026 (Thursday the 15th). My rent app charges a fee when I pay by card. The app is run by a payments company my agent uses, and it's that company that charges the card fee. There's also a manual bank transfer option with no fee, but it's slower. Can the app charge me the card fee? Does it matter whether the fee goes to the app company or to the agent?
answer:
**Short answer:** Probably not. Under the Act, the app cannot charge a card fee for paying rent unless an exception applies, and the documents I found don't identify one. Who receives the fee doesn't change that.

**Versions applied:** The Residential Tenancies Act 1997 (version 111, in force from 25 November 2025 to 29 June 2026) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf) and the Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021 (version 005, in force from 25 November 2025 to 9 February 2026) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf) both apply on 15 January 2026.

### What the law says

- **Fee-free method must be available.** The rental provider or agent must ensure a rent payment method that incurs no additional costs (other than the renter's own bank or account fees) is reasonably available [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Electronic payment fees are banned.** A person must not demand or receive a charge in relation to the establishment or use of "any other electronic payment facility for payment of rent" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The penalty is 60 penalty units [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). This wording covers any person, not just the agent.
- **Bank transfer counts.** Electronic funds transfer is the prescribed payment method [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf), so the manual bank transfer option is a lawful, fee-free method.
- **Disclosure.** Before you agree to a payment method, the provider or agent must tell you about costs, including third-party transaction fees and electronic payment facility fees [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Fee prohibition for rent payment.** A business other than the provider, the agent or an authorised deposit-taking institution must not demand or receive a fee for prescribed matters relating to rent payment [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The regulations list "rent payment (other than payment surcharge fees permitted under any other Act)" as a prescribed matter [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

### Does it matter who gets the fee?

- **For the general ban, no.** The electronic payment facility ban applies to any person [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf), so the fee is prohibited whether it goes to the app company or the agent.
- **For the fee-prohibition provision, yes.** That provision exempts the provider and agent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf), so it applies to the app company but not to the agent. However, the rent-payment prescribed matter in the regulations [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf) does not take effect until 31 March 2026 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). So it doesn't apply on 15 January 2026.
- **Caveat:** The documents don't identify any other Act that permits a payment surcharge, so I can't confirm that exception applies.

### What you can do

1. **Pay by bank transfer.** It's fee-free apart from your own bank fees and is a method the law recognises [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).
2. **Ask the agent in writing** whether the card fee is charged by the agent, the app company, or both, and request the cost information the agent must give before you agree to a payment method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
3. **Ask the agent to confirm** that a fee-free payment method is available to you [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
4. **Get more information** from Consumer Affairs Victoria's renting resources, which the regulations reference [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

### Gaps in the documents

- The excerpts don't say what happens if a payment method is slower. They don't define "reasonably available."
- They don't set out a complaint or dispute process for payment fees.
- The regulation provision on rent-payment fees (reg 21C) only applies from 31 March 2026 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). The later version isn't in the documents, so I can't say how it will read then.

question: This is happening now, on 15 October 2019. I signed a lease and picked up the keys, but before moving in I found damp, mould and rotting timber in the house. I haven't moved any of my things in or stayed there yet. What are my options? Can I cancel, ask for repairs, or ask for lower rent?
answer:
**Short answer:** The Act gives you a right to end the agreement before you move in, but only on specific grounds and by a written notice. It also gives you repair remedies. The retrieved text does not clearly give you a right to a rent reduction for these defects.

## What the law says on 15 October 2019

The relevant text is the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* (No. 109 of 1997), Authorised Version No. 088, in force from 2 July 2019 to 3 December 2019, so it applies on today's date [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

- **Condition on entry:** On the agreed day to move in, the landlord must ensure the premises are vacant and in a reasonably clean condition. You are not required to move into premises that don't comply, and you pay no rent from the agreed entry day until you actually move in [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Repairs:** The landlord must ensure the premises are maintained in good repair [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Mould and damp:** The definition of "urgent repairs" includes "the presence of mould or damp caused by or related to the building structure" where it makes the premises unsafe or insecure [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Notice of damage:** You must give the landlord written notice "as soon as practicable" after becoming aware of damage [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

## What you can do

**1. Cancel**
- You can terminate if you have not entered into possession and you give notice of termination on the ground that the premises are "not in good repair" or "unfit for human habitation" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- Separately, you may give a notice of intention to vacate if the premises are unfit for human habitation. That notice may specify a termination date that is the day it is given or a later date [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- The notice must be in writing and signed by you or your agent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Gaps:** The excerpts don't define "unfit for human habitation" or "entered into possession." It is unclear whether picking up the keys counts as possession, and whether damp, mould and rotting timber meet the "unfit" test. The excerpts also don't state a notice period for the pre-possession termination.

**2. Ask for repairs**
- *Non-urgent repairs:* Give written notice. If the landlord doesn't carry out the repairs within 14 days, you can apply to the Director to investigate, and then to the Tribunal for an order requiring specified repairs [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The Tribunal must hear such an application within 7 days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). It can order the repairs, the use of a suitably qualified person, and compensation [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- *Urgent repairs:* You may arrange urgent repairs if you took reasonable steps to get the landlord to do them and they couldn't or wouldn't. You must give 7 days' written notice of the repairs and their cost, and the landlord must reimburse the reasonable cost within 7 days of written notice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Gap:** The excerpts don't say whether these repair remedies apply before you have taken occupation.

**3. Ask for lower rent**
- The retrieved text does not give you a clear right to reduce the rent for pre-move-in defects.
- The rent-free rule (s 65(3)) depends on the premises not being vacant and reasonably clean, and the excerpts don't say whether damp or mould falls within that [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- If you have given repair notices and the landlord fails to act, you can apply to the Tribunal to pay rent into the Rent Special Account. That holds rent but does not reduce it [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- The Act lets the Tribunal declare rent excessive, having regard to the "state of repair and general condition of the rented premises" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). However, the complaint route is tied to reduced services or a proposed rent increase, and a Tribunal application generally requires a Director's report first or leave [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). Whether this applies to a lease you have not started is not clear from these excerpts.

## Practical steps

- Photograph and document all defects now.
- Give the landlord written notice of the damp, mould and timber problems, which is what s 72AA requires [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- If you are given a condition report, a copy given to the landlord counts as notice of any defects stated in it [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). Check that the report records these defects accurately, since it is conclusive evidence of condition unless you disagree with it in writing [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- Get advice before serving any termination notice, because a defective notice can be invalid [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

**Not covered by these documents:** The retrieved material is the Act itself. I did not find the standard-form lease, the Director's guidelines, the rental minimum standards, or any text defining "unfit for human habitation." Those would affect your answer.

question: I am asking on Tuesday 8 November 2022. I signed a lease through an agency and paid the bond and the first month's rent. Now, a week after I signed, the agent says the owner will manage the place themselves and has sent me new bank details for the rent. What should I check before I pay into the new account?
answer:
**Short answer:** Under the Act, the owner cannot simply switch your rent to a new account. The change needs your agreement, and the owner must give you written notice of the change, a receipt for each payment, and a payment method that doesn't cost you extra. The documents don't cover how to verify bank details, so you'll need to check that separately.

This answer applies the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* (Authorised Version No. 101, in force 7 September 2022 to 23 May 2023) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf) and the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021* (Authorised Version No. 002, in force 1 June 2022 to 30 November 2024) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf), both in force on 8 November 2022.

## What the law says

- **Where and how rent is paid:** Rent is payable at the place in the agreement, or at the rented premises if none is specified. Otherwise it is payable in the manner specified in the agreement [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Changing the payment method:** The provider and renter may, *by agreement*, change how rent is payable [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). A change to a new account is therefore not something the owner can impose alone.
- **Costs:** The provider or agent must give you information about any costs (including third-party transaction fees) of a payment method before you consent to using it [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Free method:** The provider must ensure a payment method that incurs no additional costs (other than your bank or account fees) is reasonably available to you [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Centrepay:** The provider must permit you to pay by Centrepay [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Change of details:** If the agent is involved, the provider must give you written notice of any change in the agent's details within 7 days of the change [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The standard form repeats this: "The rental provider must notify the renter within 7 days if any of this information changes" [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).
- **Receipts:** For a payment not made in person, a written receipt must be given within 5 business days if you request one [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). It must be signed by the person receiving the payment and state your name and the premises, the date of receipt, the period paid for, the amount, and that the payment is for rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Bond:** The bond must be lodged with the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority within 10 business days of receipt [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). If you don't receive a receipt within 15 business days of paying the bond, you may email rtba@justice.vic.gov.au or call 1300 137 164 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).
- **Transfer of the owner's rights:** If the owner takes over the landlord's rights and duties from another party, the provider and the new party must notify the Authority within 5 days. The provider must also give you a copy of that notice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).

## What you can check or ask

1. **Ask for the change in writing.** Request the new details from the agent and the owner in writing, and confirm the owner is the one asking for the change.
2. **Don't treat it as settled until you agree.** You're entitled to agree or decline the change, since the Act requires agreement [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). If you agree, record that in writing.
3. **Ask about costs.** Before you use the new account, ask what fees, if any, apply, and make sure a fee-free method is still available [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
4. **Confirm the agent's status.** Ask whether the agent is still acting. If the agent is no longer acting, the owner must give you written notice of the change within 7 days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).
5. **Check the bond.** Ask the agent or owner whether the bond was lodged with the Authority, and check for the receipt. question: Today is Wednesday 3 December 2025. - **Entry:** A landlord or agent may enter "at any time between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. on any day (except a public holiday)" to carry out a duty under the Act, if "at least 24 hours notice has been given" [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Your notice of seven days meets that minimum, and 10 am to 12:30 pm falls inside the 8 am to 6 pm window.
- **Notice requirements:** The notice must be in writing, state why entry is wanted, and be given by post or delivered personally between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

The entrant must act "in a reasonable manner" and must not stay longer than necessary without your consent [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

question: It's the middle of January 2026 (Thursday the 15th). My rent app charges a fee when I pay by card. The app is run by a payments company my agent uses, and it's that company that charges the card fee. There's also a manual bank transfer option with no fee, but it's slower. Can the app charge me the card fee? Does it matter whether the fee goes to the app company or to the agent?
answer:
**Short answer:** Probably not, if the agent is the one who makes a fee-free method available. The documents say the agent must ensure a no-extra-cost payment method is reasonably available, but they don't clearly settle whether the payments company's card fee is itself banned as of 15 January 2026.

I've applied the versions in force on that date: the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* (Authorised Version No. 111, in force from 25 November 2025) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf) and the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021* (Authorised Version No. 005, in force from 25 November 2025 to 9 February 2026) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

## What the law says

- **Fee-free method must be available.** A provider or agent "must ensure that a rent payment method that incurs no additional costs (other than bank fees or account fees payable on the renter's bank account) is reasonably available to the renter." The penalty is 80 penalty units for a natural person or 400 for a body corporate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Cost information before you choose a method.** The provider or agent "must give the renter information about any costs (including third party transaction fees, direct debit dishonour fees and any other electronic payment facility fees) that the renter may incur by using a particular payment method before the renter consents to use the payment method" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Bank transfer counts.** The prescribed payment method is electronic funds transfer [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). The provider or agent must also permit Centrepay [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Prohibited terms.** A tenancy agreement term requiring rent to be paid in advance by a method that requires additional costs (other than bank or account fees on the renter's account) is a prescribed prohibited term [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).
- **Fees charged by businesses.** Section 51A says a business other than a provider, agent, or authorised deposit-taking institution must not demand or receive a fee for a prescribed matter relating to "the payment of rent" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The prescribed matters are in regulation 21C, which "has effect on and after 31 March 2026." That list includes "rent payment (other than payment surcharge fees permitted under any other Act)" [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

## Your questions

**Can the app charge the card fee?** The documents don't give a clear answer for 15 January 2026. Regulation 21C, which would make a rent-payment fee prohibited under section 51A, doesn't take effect until 31 March 2026 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). Also, the excerpt I retrieved doesn't show when section 51A itself commenced [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Separately, the agent's obligation to offer a fee-free method applies now [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). If the agent is making the card option the only practical way to pay, that is the stronger point to raise.

**Does it matter whether the fee goes to the app company or the agent?** Yes, in two ways:

- **If the agent receives the fee:** the agent is covered by the fee-free-method duty and the cost-disclosure duty [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Section 51A does not apply to agents [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **If the app company keeps the fee:** the documents don't say whether the company is liable under the agent's duties. Section 51A does reach businesses other than providers, agents, and deposit-taking institutions [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf), but as noted above its rent-payment prescribed matter is not in force until 31 March 2026 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

## What you can do or ask

1. **Ask the agent in writing** whether a no-extra-cost method (such as bank transfer) is available and whether it is reasonably available to you [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
2. **Ask for the card fee amount** and any other electronic payment fees before you choose the card option, since the agent must give that information before you consent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
3. **Pay by bank transfer** if the card fee is the only difference. The documents treat electronic funds transfer as a prescribed method [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). Your own bank fees are excluded from the fee-free requirement [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
4. **Ask for a receipt.** If you request one at the time of payment, it must be given within 5 business days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The receipt must state your name and the rented premises, the date, the period paid for, the amount, and that the payment is for rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
5. **Check your agreement.** A clause requiring card payment with extra costs may be a prohibited term [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

**Not covered by the documents:** how to complain or enforce these rules, and whether the app company is directly liable under section 42. Also, the regulations version I retrieved ends on 9 February 2026 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf), so I can't tell you what applies after that date.

question: This is happening now, on 15 October 2019. I signed a lease and picked up the keys, but before moving in I found damp, mould and rotting timber in the house. I haven't moved any of my things in or stayed there yet. What are my options? Can I cancel, ask for repairs, or ask for lower rent?
answer:
**Short answer:** Under the retrieved Act, you can probably refuse to move in and give notice to end the agreement, and you may be able to get the landlord to make repairs. The documents do not clearly give you a right to a rent reduction before you move in, but you are not required to pay rent for the period before you actually move in.

**Document and version:** The retrieved document is the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* (No. 109 of 1997), version 088 (rta-1997-v088), which the metadata shows was in force from 2 July 2019 to 3 December 2019, so it covers 15 October 2019 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The document does not use the words "Authorised Version," so I am relying on the version number in its metadata.

---

### What the law says

- **Condition on the day you take occupation:** The landlord must ensure the premises are vacant and reasonably clean on the agreed day you enter occupation. If they are not, you are not required to move in [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **No rent for that period:** If the premises do not comply, you do not have to pay rent from the agreed occupation day until the day you actually move in [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Minimum standards:** The landlord must ensure the premises comply with the prescribed rental minimum standards on or before the day you enter occupation, and must comply with them on or immediately after that day [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The document does not set out what those standards say, so I cannot confirm whether damp, mould or rotting timber breaches them.
- **Repairs duty:** The landlord must keep the premises "in good repair" and "in a reasonably fit and suitable condition for occupation." This applies whether or not you knew of the disrepair before moving in [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Mould, damp and structure:** "Urgent repairs" includes any fault that makes premises unsafe or insecure, including "the presence of mould or damp caused by or related to the building structure" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). Whether your rotting timber and mould fit this depends on the facts.

### Your options

**1. Cancel (end the agreement before moving in)**
- You can give notice if you have not entered possession and the premises are "not in good repair" or "unfit for human habitation," or do not "meet any rental minimum standards" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- The agreement then terminates [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- The document does not state a notice period for this ground.

**2. Ask for repairs**
- You must give the landlord written notice of damage or breakdowns as soon as practicable after becoming aware of them [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Urgent repairs:** If you have taken reasonable steps to get the landlord to repair immediately and they cannot or do not, you may arrange the repairs yourself. You must give the landlord 7 days' written notice of the repairs and their cost. The landlord must reimburse the reasonable cost within 7 days of receiving written notice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The earlier $1,000 cap has been removed in this version [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Tribunal:** You can apply to the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal (the Tribunal) for an order requiring urgent repairs [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Non-urgent repairs:** You can give written notice, and if the landlord does not carry out the repairs within 14 days, you can ask the Director to investigate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). You can also apply to the Tribunal for an order requiring repairs [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

**3. Ask for lower rent**
- The document does not give you a general right to a rent reduction before moving in.
- The rent-free period in section 65(3) (above) is the closest provision [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- The Tribunal can order compensation in the form of a refund or reduction of rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- A Rent Special Account order is available only after you have given a repair notice and the landlord has failed to comply [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- The excessive-rent provisions apply to rent increases or reduced services, not to the condition of premises at the start of a lease [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

---

### What the documents do not cover
- The rental minimum standards themselves, which would show whether your damp, mould or timber problems breach them.
- The notice period for cancelling under section 91L.
- Whether your lease is in the standard form, or any terms about repairs or cancellation in your specific agreement.
- Any Tribunal fees or timeframes beyond those quoted above.

**Practical next steps:** Put your complaint in writing to the landlord or agent now, with photos and a description of the damp, mould and timber. Keep copies. Get a written report from a suitably qualified person if you can. Then consider whether to give a written notice of termination or a notice requiring repairs. For a decision on whether to cancel, it would be worth speaking to a tenancy advice service, such as Consumer Affairs Victoria or a community legal centre.

question: I am asking on Tuesday 8 November 2022. I signed a lease through an agency and paid the bond and the first month's rent. Now, a week after I signed, the agent says the owner will manage the place themselves and has sent me new bank details for the rent. What should I check before I pay into the new account?
answer:
**Short answer:** Don't pay the new account until the owner has confirmed the change in writing and the change is agreed under your lease. Based on the documents, a unilateral change of bank details isn't clearly allowed.

**Applicable law (as at 8 November 2022):** I'm relying on the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997*, version 101 (in force 7 September 2022 to 23 May 2023), and the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021*, version 002 (in force 1 June 2022 to 30 November 2024) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).

## What the law says

- **Payment place and method:** Rent is payable at the place specified in the agreement, or at the rented premises if none is specified. Otherwise it's payable in the manner specified in the agreement [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Changing the payment method:** The provider and renter, *by agreement*, may change the manner in which rent is payable [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Fees:** The provider or agent must ensure a payment method that incurs no additional costs (other than your bank or account fees) is reasonably available. The penalty is 60 penalty units [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). They must also give you information about any costs (including third-party transaction fees) before you consent to a payment method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Centrepay:** The provider must permit payment by Centrepay [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Receipts:** If you pay other than in person and request a receipt, it must be given within 5 business days. It must be signed by the person receiving payment and state your name and the rented premises, the date of receipt, the period paid for, the amount, and that the payment is for rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Notice of changes:** The provider must give you written notice of any change in the agent or provider details (name, address for service, and phone or facsimile numbers) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Bond:** The provider holds your bond on trust until it is paid to the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority. They must lodge it within 10 business days, with a completed bond lodgment form [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf). You must sign the form, and they must give you a copy [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Transfer of rights:** If the provider transfers their rights and duties under the agreement to another person and a bond has been paid, both must notify the Authority within 5 days, and the provider must give you a copy of that notice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).

## What you can check or ask

1. **Ask for written confirmation of the change**, including the new owner's full name and address for service of documents, and their contact details [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
2. **Check whether the change is agreed.** Under the Act, a change in how rent is paid requires agreement between you and the provider [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The documents don't say whether a change of account by the owner alone counts as a change of payment method, so ask the owner to confirm in writing that you agree to it.
3. **Check the fees.** Ask whether the new account incurs any costs for you, and confirm a fee-free method is available [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
4. **Check the bond.** Ask whether the owner is taking over the bond and whether a transfer notice to the Authority is needed [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). If you haven't received a bond receipt within 15 business days of paying, you can contact the Authority at rtba@justice.vic.gov.au or 1300 137 164 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).
5. **Ask for a receipt** for each rent payment, and request one in writing if you don't pay in person [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
6. **Keep records** of the agent's notices and all payments.

## What the documents don't cover

- Whether the agent still has authority to change payment details, or what happens if the owner takes over the tenancy. The documents only require agents to produce evidence of their authority when the Authority asks [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- How to verify bank details or avoid payment scams. Independently checking the account details with the owner through a phone number you already have is general good practice, not something in these documents.
